text.offer: There you are, love. You came to in the dormitory, same as the rest of them, and nobody can tell you why, least of all me. The levy took our lay brothers for the war in the gap, so I'm afraid you're our lay brother now. Keeper Brannick's out on the road. He'll want to see if you can hold a stick.
text.summary: Find Keeper Brannick on the road outside the Abbey's front door.
text.done: So you're the new one. On your feet, sleeper. Let's see what you're good for.

text.offer: Foxes. Up from the west shore every night, after the hens. Lay brothers used to sit up with them. No lay brothers now. Go down the shore and kill six. Don't come back with feathers in your teeth.
text.summary: Kill 6 foxes on the lakeshore west of the Abbey.
text.waiting: Six. I'm counting the hens, sleeper.
text.done: Six. Good. You'll do. I'll stop calling you sleeper. Probably.

text.offer: Hold this. No, the other end. The chapel's candles keep walking off, so I make rushlights: lamp rush, peeled, dipped in fat. Burns near as well and nobody wants to steal it. The rushes grow along the shore below us. Eight good ones, the tall green kind, not the brown.
text.summary: Cut 8 lamp rushes along the lakeshore below the Abbey.
text.waiting: Lamp rush. Tall and green. Brown's no use.
text.done: Lovely. These'll keep the chapel lit a week. Now, where did I put the fat.

text.offer: Aubin. I keep the Wakers' dreams, and write them down. You've seen the wisps? Over the falls pool, drifting... More every year, I think. Or am I counting wrong? Bring me some of their light. Six glimmers. They give them up when they come apart. I'd like to know what they're made of before...
text.summary: Bring 6 wisp-glimmers from the dream-wisps over the falls pool.
text.waiting: Any glimmers yet? They'll be cold. They always are.
text.done: Cold. No weight at all. Like something remembered rather than... Never mind. Thank you.

text.offer: Aubin wants a sleeping draught for you, and that means dreamroot. Pale thing, grows in the falls pool's shallows and nowhere else. I'd go myself, but those wisps make my skin crawl. Five roots. Pull them whole.
text.summary: Pull 5 dreamroot from the falls pool's shallows.
text.waiting: Whole roots, mind. A broken one's no good to me.
text.done: Five. Smell that? Rain on stone. That's the Dream's water, Aubin says. I just call it dreamroot.

text.offer: Soon I'll ask you to sleep by the water, for your first dream. Before I do... Have you heard of Brother Ansel? No. Well. The Abbess tells it better than I would. Ask her, at the nave door. His stone's in the graveyard behind the nave, the one with the cross.
text.summary: Ask Abbess Corra about Brother Ansel.
text.done: Ansel. He kept the dreams before Aubin, thirty years back. One night he walked into the falls pool in his sleep and didn't come out. We never found him, love. So when Aubin puts you down by that water, you wake up when he says. Promise me.

text.offer: Every Waker has a first dream. I keep a book of them... Here. Nell's draught. Drink it on the flat stone at the falls pool's edge, and sleep. Then come and tell me what you saw. Will you?
text.summary: Drink Nell's draught on the flat stone at the falls pool's edge, then tell Aubin what you dreamed.
text.waiting: The flat stone, at the water's edge. Did you sleep?
text.done: You've gone pale. Water, was it? And falling... Yes. They all dream that now, every one this year. Something listening, you say? That's new. I'll write it down.

objectives.text: Slept on the stone by the falls pool
objectives.doneText: You lie down on the cold stone and drink. The draught tastes of rain. Water closes over you, and you're falling, slowly, through a dark that glows. Far below, something is listening. Then the falls are loud, and you're awake, wet with spray.

text.offer: You've done everything this old place can teach you, love, and some things it shouldn't have. The Hallams are our neighbours west along the north shore, at Hallam's cross. We owe them for seed barley, and I can't pay in coin. Take Wenna Hallam these rushlights. Tell her they're from me, and that I'm sorry it isn't more.
text.summary: Take the bundle of rushlights to Wenna Hallam at Hallam's cross.
text.waiting: Hallam's cross is west along the shore road. You can't miss the shrine.
text.done: Rushlights from the Abbess. She owes us for barley, and she sends what she has. That's more than some do. Welcome to Hallam's cross.

text.offer: The Council's assessor is here, Pell Duvane, to count our stores for the tithe. He seems an honest man. But the Council's rule is a tenth of what is there, and I would like the Abbey to know what is there before anyone else tells us. Would you count the stores for us? The barrels, the crates and the big crate, up the tower. Then Duvane and I can compare.
text.summary: Count the barrel stack, the crate stack and the large crate in the Abbey's stores, for Abbess Corra.
text.waiting: The barrels, the crates, and the big crate up the tower. Take your time. The assessor's knee is in no hurry.
text.done: Good. That matches what the keepers told me, and I will give it to Duvane myself. If his count differs, we will know which of us to believe.

objectives.text: Large crate counted, up the tower

text.offer: That assessor. Limps like a three-legged dog. I don't care for the Council, but I'll not watch a man hobble. Comfrey and arnica, that tin. Give it him for the knee. And don't say it's from me.
text.summary: Take Nell's salve to Assessor Pell Duvane.
text.waiting: Well? Go on. Before I change my mind.
text.done: For the knee? That's kind. Very kind. Who should I thank? No? Then I'll thank you, and perhaps you'll pass it along.

text.offer: There are fish in the falls pool's shallows now. Pale ones, with no eyes. There never were before... were there? I'd like four for the book, beside the first dreams. Mind your fingers. They bite.
text.summary: Bring 4 pale fish from the eyeless fry in the falls pool's shallows.
text.waiting: No eyes at all. Did you notice? What would need eyes, down there?
text.done: Smooth where the eyes should be. Something breeds these. Something in the water. How big, I wonder?

text.offer: The chapel's candles. Kobold sneaks, from burrows in the cliff's north end. They creep in at night and take them. Beeswax, bought dear, and the Council's assessor has every one on his list. Go up there. Kill sneaks. Bring back six candles.
text.summary: Kill kobold sneaks at their burrows in the cliff's north end and bring back 6 stolen candles.
text.waiting: Watch for them. They hide till they're on you.
text.done: Chewed, some of them. Still beeswax. The assessor can count them twice for all I care.

text.offer: The sneaks answer to a fat one. Tallowtooth, they call him. Sits on the candles in the deepest burrow with a glass lantern. While he's got a hoard to grow, they'll keep stealing for it. Go in. Kill him. Bring me the lantern.
text.summary: Kill Tallowtooth in the deepest of the sneaks' burrows and bring back his glass lantern.
text.waiting: Deepest burrow. Follow the smell of tallow.
text.done: That's the lantern? Huh. Better glass than ours. Keep the sneaks hungry for a while, that will.

text.offer: This was in with the candles you brought back. Glows on its own. Kobolds don't make glass like that. Kobolds don't make glass. Take it to Aubin. He knows old things.
text.summary: Take the glowing shard to Keeper Aubin.
text.waiting: Aubin's down by the dock. Usually.
text.done: Oh. Oh, this is old. Elves' glass, from the Age of Light... Kobolds didn't make it. They found it. Somewhere deep in the cliff, carried out... Where are they digging?

text.offer: If the Abbess sent you, you're welcome. If she didn't, you're still welcome, if you'll work. Start in the big barn, behind the house. Rats. Every sack they open is a sack short when the collector comes, and we're short enough. The cat won't go in. Kill eight.
text.summary: Kill 8 barn rats in the Hallams' big barn, behind their farmhouse.
text.waiting: Eight. I can hear them from here.
text.done: Quieter. Good. That's eight sacks I won't have to explain.

text.offer: Boars come down off the rise at night and root up the barley, east of the cross along the Abbey road. A row a night, near enough. And the cart cover's in rags. Bring me five hides, and I'm rid of both troubles.
text.summary: Bring 5 boar hides from the boars in the barley, east of the cross along the Abbey road.
text.waiting: Five hides. Whole ones, if you can.
text.done: Good hides. Orla will scrape them, and the cart goes covered to Brightford.

text.offer: The young boars follow an old one. Old Bristle, Grandfather calls him. He breaks the hedges to let them through, and he wallows at the edge of the rise, west of here off the Brightford road. Kill him and the rest will keep to the woods. Grandfather wants the tusks over the door. I want the hedges whole.
text.summary: Kill Old Bristle in his wallow at the edge of the rise, west off the Brightford road, and bring back his tusks.
text.waiting: He's big, and he's old. Old means clever.
text.done: Those are his. Grandfather will tell you how he nearly had him once, in the old lord's day. Let him. It's a long story, but it's mostly true.

text.offer: Varn Ostrey weighs the tithe at Brightford, for the Council. His scales say we owe another cart. Our sacks are full. I filled them. But a Hallam saying so is farmers' lying, to the reeve. Weigh three of them on our steelyard, in the big barn. You aren't a Hallam. You'll say what you saw.
text.summary: Weigh 3 of the Hallams' tithe sacks on the steelyard in their big barn.
text.waiting: Three sacks. Read the beam, not my face.
text.done: Full. You saw it. Then Varn's scales are wrong, or Varn is. I'd like to know which.

objectives.text: Tithe sacks weighed on the steelyard
objectives.doneText: Each time, the beam swings, then settles level at the Council's mark, with grain to spare. The sacks are full.

text.offer: The reeve at Brightford keeps the Council's true weight. Odile Marchbank. I don't trust her. I trust Varn less. Take her my letter, and this sack, sealed, so she can weigh it herself. And tell her you saw the others weighed. Brightford's south-west, down the Brightford road, past the rise.
text.summary: Take Wenna's letter and the sealed tithe sack to Reeve Odile Marchbank in Brightford, south-west down the Brightford road.
text.waiting: Down the Brightford road, past the rise. Don't let anyone open that sack.
text.done: A letter from Wenna Hallam. She writes only when she is angry, and she is seldom wrong when she is. You saw her sacks weighed, and they were full? Then I will not take her word, or yours. I will test Varn's scales myself.

text.offer: Ah, a strong back! In the old lord's day we'd have had six of you up the hedges by now, and a cask broached by dark, and my cousin Abel singing... Well. Hedge apples. Little hard sour things, wild in the hedges along the roads east of here. Make the best cider there is. And the Council's collector has no column for cider. Never has. Funny, that. Ten, if you would. My back won't do the high branches.
text.summary: Gather 10 hedge apples from the hedges along the roads east and north-east of the cross.
text.waiting: The small sour ones. Sweet apples are for eating, and that's no use to anybody.
text.done: Lovely. Hard as stones and twice as sour. Come spring they'll be the best thing this side of the gap, and not a penny of tithe on them.

text.offer: Now, here's a thing. Some mornings there's a sack of grain on our step. Good grain. Nobody sees who leaves it, and Wenna won't hear of asking. But the Council will ask, sooner or later, where a farm that's short finds spare grain. Whoever it is comes and goes by the hedge gap behind the shrine. Have a look there, would you? Bring me whatever you find.
text.summary: Search the hedge gap behind the wayside shrine at the crossroads, and bring Tobin what you find.
text.waiting: Behind the shrine. Where the bluebells are trodden down.
text.done: Grey wool. Close-woven... That's Tennely grey, or I'm a turnip. A kindness from the old days, that's all it is. No, I'll not say more. And neither will you, if you're wise.

text.offer: We graze the sheep down by Crumbling Ruin in summer, out west at the rise's south-west foot. Did, I should say. Two ewes last year, wrapped up and hung like hams. Spiders. The ruin's full of their webs. Take this torch and burn out the nests, five of them, and I'll put the flock back. I'd go myself, but my knees have opinions.
text.summary: Burn 5 web nests in and round Crumbling Ruin, west at the rise's south-west foot, with Tobin's torch.
text.waiting: Burn them right through. Half a web's a whole spider.
text.done: All five? Then the sheep go down next week. That ruin was old when I was a boy, you know, and my grandfather never knew what it had been. Something holy, he thought. Holy or not, it's ours to graze.

text.offer: Farmers up the road say the tithe collector's scales weigh their sacks light. Farmers have said so since there were scales. But I will not accuse a man on a farmer's word, nor dismiss one on a collector's. This is the Council's standard, the true weight a sack must match. Varn Ostrey's scales stand in the tithe barn, east of the inn. He takes his supper at Moll's at this hour. Weigh the standard on his scales, and tell me what they read.
text.summary: Weigh the Council's standard on Varn's scales in the tithe barn, east of the inn, and tell the reeve what they read.
text.waiting: The standard, on his scales. Then come back and tell me plainly.
text.done: A tenth light. A tenth, exactly. That is not wear, or damp, or a bent beam. Someone set them so.

objectives.text: The standard weighed on Varn's scales
objectives.doneText: You set the brass weight in the pan. The beam swings and settles, and the mark reads a tenth short of what the weight is stamped. You try it twice more. A tenth short, each time.

text.offer: Light scales on one farm is a quarrel. Light scales on every farm is a crime, and one I can take to the Council. There are three farms between the road and the river, east of town: the Pellows, the Fairleys and Tamsin Ware. Ask each of them what Varn's scales made of their sacks.
text.summary: Ask the 3 farms between the road and the river, east of Brightford, what Varn's scales made of their sacks.
text.waiting: Three farms, east along the road. Ask, and listen. Don't tell them what you found.
text.done: A tenth, from every one of them. Then it is not a mistake, and it was never only the Hallams.

objectives.doneText: Agnes Pellow wipes her hands on her apron. "Short? Every year since the Council came. Varn says a tenth for the sacks' weight, and a tenth it is. Twelve sacks, counted as eleven."
Hob Fairley spits. "I told the reeve last spring. Twenty sacks in, eighteen on his ledger. Said I'd packed them loose. I've packed sacks forty years."
Tamsin Ware frowns at her fingers. "Fifteen I filled, and paid on thirteen and a half. I thought I'd counted wrong. Have I not?"

text.offer: A tenth from every farm in the heartland is a great deal of grain. It went somewhere. Varn writes down everything, and he keeps his ledger in his desk in the tithe barn. If I ask him for it, I give him a night to make it say whatever he likes, and whoever set his scales a night to warn him. Copy it out for me, every page, while he's at Moll's. Leave it as you found it.
text.summary: Copy Varn's ledger at his desk in the tithe barn, while he's at the inn, and bring the reeve the copy.
text.waiting: His desk, at the back of the tithe barn. Every page, and put it back as it lay.
text.done: Every sack, and the extra tenth in its own column. All of it loaded onto the grain wagons to Tennely Hall, "by order." By whose order, he doesn't say. Varn never asks whose.

text.offer: I could put Varn in the lock-up. And whoever set his scales would sleep easier for it, because a clerk in a cell is a clerk who's been made to say what he's told. No. He's to keep the Abbey's books, with Assessor Duvane, well away from here. Take him my order. He's at Moll's.
text.summary: Take the reeve's order to Varn Ostrey at Moll's inn: he's to keep the Abbey's books with Assessor Duvane.
text.waiting: He'll be at Moll's, at the corner table. Be kind to him. He'll be frightened.
text.done: The Abbey? I'm... not to be... Oh. Oh, thank you. I didn't, I never, I only set them as I was told. The order came with the scales. I never asked. One doesn't ask. I'll go tonight.

quests.name: Grey Coats on the North Road

text.offer: Robbers on the north road. Grey coats. Greycoats, the old lord's men, gone bandit since the revolution. They've stopped two carts this month, and if the grain wagons stop, the town eats bark. Take the left fork north of town. Their camp's in the trees west of the road, a good walk up. Half my lads are at the gap. You're not. Clear them out, and bring me those notched sticks they all carry. Five. I want to know what they're counting.
text.summary: Kill the grey-coated robbers at their camp west of the north road, the left fork north of town,, and bring back 5 of their notched sticks.
text.waiting: North road, camp in the trees. Five sticks.
text.done: Notches. Rows of them. Carts, maybe, or days. Can't read it. Doesn't matter. Fewer robbers is fewer robbers.

text.offer: You fought the robbers on the north road. Then you have seen their coats. I wore the grey for thirty years, for the old lord. Those are not Greycoats. And there is a man in the lock-up, Jory Venn, taken for a robbery he did not do, who can prove it. Bring him one of their coats. He will show you.
text.summary: Take a robber's grey coat from the camp on the north road to Jory Venn in the lock-up, by the militia post.
text.waiting: A coat from one of them. Jory is in the lock-up, by the militia post, west of the road.
text.done: Give it here. Ha. Feel that? Thin. And the grey's wrong, see, too blue. Tennely grey is dyed with alder, it goes brown in the rain. And the cut: ours button left over right. Somebody made this to look like us, from a description. Someone wants the Greycoats blamed.

text.offer: Those robbers aren't after carts. They're after the grain wagons to Tennely Hall, and they want it pinned on us. The granary's captain, Wystan Hale, wore the grey once. He'll listen, if it comes from me. Take him this. Up the road to Hallam's cross, then north on the grain road, the way the wagons go. And don't read it. I'd know.
text.summary: Take Jory's message to Captain Wystan Hale at Tennely Hall, north of Hallam's cross up the grain road.
text.waiting: Captain Hale, at Tennely Hall. Nobody else.
text.done: Jory Venn. In a cell, and still sending me orders. Hm. False coats, and they want my wagons. Then they'll come here before long. I'm glad you brought this. I'll need you.

text.offer: The granary at Tennely Hall's short of guards, with robbers about. Can't spare mine. You'll do. Up the road to Hallam's cross, then north on the grain road. Report to Captain Hale. Old Greycoat himself, mind. But he keeps the grain safe.
text.summary: Go to Tennely Hall, north of Hallam's cross up the grain road, and report to Captain Wystan Hale.
text.waiting: Hallam's cross, then the grain road north. Captain Hale.
text.done: Pike sent you? Then she's worried, and she's not a worrier. Good. Stay. There's work.

text.offer: Sweetheart, you look hungry, and I've nothing to feed you! My eel pie's the best this side of the gap, and my eel man went with the levy. The ford's full of eels, just east of town where the road crosses. Six, love, and you'll eat like a lord. Well. Like a reeve.
text.summary: Bring Moll 6 eels from the ford, just east of town.
text.waiting: Six eels, my duck. They bite, mind.
text.done: Look at them! Pie tonight, and you'll have the first slice. Don't tell the sergeant, she thinks she gets the first slice.

text.offer: Wolves in the woods south of town. They go for travellers coming over the crags. I've no lads for it. I pay by the pelt. Six.
text.summary: Bring Sergeant Pike 6 wolf pelts from the woods south of town.
text.waiting: Six pelts. South woods.
text.done: Six. Paid. Road's safer. Next.

text.offer: "Raised by the people of Tennelford, to the Tennelys, who kept this ford." That's what it says. I know it by heart. I never loved them, mind. But this town was Tennelford for a hundred years, and Ludo Crake means to buy that plaque off the Council for the weight of its bronze. I asked Odile, and she's given leave for it to hang in the reeve's hall instead. Only my hands won't manage a crowbar. Take it down off the plinth for me, before Ludo's offer comes through.
text.summary: Take the plaque down from the old lord's toppled statue in the square, with the reeve's leave, before Ludo Crake can buy it.
text.waiting: Off the plinth, gently. Odile's said yes, and I won't give her the chance to change her mind.
text.done: There. "To the Tennelys, who kept this ford." They did keep it, whatever else they did. It'll hang in the reeve's hall. Ludo can have the statue's toes.

text.offer: See this? A shrine bell, good bronze. The militia sold it me for the war in the gap. Thing is, I sell by weight, and nobody'll buy a bell everybody knows came off the Hallams' shrine. So: I'll trade it for its weight in iron. The robbers have left wrecked carts all down the north road, and Sergeant Pike's posted them as salvage for whoever clears them off the road. Tyres, hinges, nails. Six lots. Bargain of the year.
text.summary: Clear 6 wrecked carts off the north road, as Sergeant Pike's salvage, and bring Ludo the iron.
text.waiting: Six lots of iron, off the carts on the north road. Pike wants them off the road anyway. Mind the robbers.
text.done: Lovely. Good, honest salvage, and the road's clear besides. Pike owes you a drink. The bell's yours. Pleasure doing business.

text.offer: Here's your bell. Glad to see the back of it, honestly. Gives me the eye. Take it back to the Hallams, at the cross up the road north-east. The old man, Tobin. He'll know it.
text.summary: Take the shrine bell back to Grandsire Tobin Hallam at Hallam's cross, north-east up the Brightford road.
text.waiting: Hallam's cross, up the road. The old man.
text.done: Well, I never. That's our bell. I rang it for the old lord's wedding, you know, before you were born, before your mother was born. Rang it so hard the rope broke. Back on the shrine it goes, and I'll ring it gently this time.

text.offer: Petal, the loggers drinking in my corner say Cliffside camp needs hands. The Council's timber quota's due, and somebody's shooting arrows at them off the cliff top. They're a good lot, loggers. Drink like fish. Go east past Hallam's cross to the camp under the cliffs, and ask for Gus Tarrant, the foreman.
text.summary: Go east past Hallam's cross to Cliffside camp, under the cliffs, and talk to Foreman Gus Tarrant.
text.waiting: East past the cross, under the cliffs. Gus Tarrant, big fellow, shouts a lot.
text.done: Moll sent you? Bless her. Yes, we need hands. Badly.

text.offer: I burn shells for lime, to whitewash the plaques in the graveyard. Every name in it is going grey. The lad who gathered my shells went with the levy, and since then the crabs have come right up the coast meadows. West of town, along the river road to the sea. Eight shells, please. Whole ones.
text.summary: Bring Hettie 8 crab shells from the crabs on the coast meadows, west of town along the river road.
text.waiting: Eight shells. Whole, mind, not cracked.
text.done: Lovely. The kiln goes on tomorrow. A town that lets its names go grey forgets them.

text.offer: I cut cress along the river, east of town, in the meadows past the farms. I sell it at the ford. An old soldier must do something. But toads have taken the beds. Great fat ones, big as dogs. Kill eight of them, and an old man will be in your debt.
text.summary: Kill 8 giant toads in the river meadows east of town, past the farms.
text.waiting: Eight toads. In the river meadows, east, past the farms.
text.done: Eight. Then the cress will come back by spring. The old lord had a taste for it, you know. Took it with his eggs.

text.offer: See that hole in the cliff foot, east of camp? Kobolds. Dug in last spring, and every night since they come out and take something. A lamp. An axe. A whole barrel of nails once, and what a kobold wants with nails I couldn't tell you. The Council's quota won't wait while I send to Brightford for new axes. Thin them out for me.
text.summary: Kill 8 kobold diggers outside the diggings, in the cliff foot east of Cliffside camp.
text.waiting: They come out round the mouth of the hole. Can't miss it, they've hung our own lamps on posts.
text.done: Eight. That'll keep them in their hole a night or two. Now I've seen what they're carrying, though, I want to know what's in there.

text.offer: Dell found one dead by the brook this morning, and it had a shard of glass on a string round its neck. Glowing. On its own. Like the old windows at the Abbey. If that's what they're digging for, there's more of it in that cliff than anyone knows, and the Council will want it before we've hauled another log. I want to know first. Bring me what the ones inside are carrying.
text.summary: Bring 8 glowing shards from the glowdiggers inside the diggings.
text.waiting: Inside, mind. The ones out front only carry what they stole from us.
text.done: Eight shards, and every one glowing. That's not a seam they've struck. That's someone's window, broken up small. Somebody built in that cliff, long before any of us.

text.offer: Ossie went in after a stolen saw. Came out white as flour. Says in the north tunnel they've built little heaps of the glass, with our lamps and axes and saws piled round them, and they bow to them. Bow! To our tools! And they fought him hardest right there. Pull those shrines apart and fetch our gear back. Kobolds with nothing to bow to might just lose heart and keep to their holes.
text.summary: Pull apart 3 shrines in the north tunnel of the diggings, and take back the camp's stolen tools.
text.waiting: The north tunnel, Ossie says. Left past the first bend. Bring the saws if you can carry them.
text.done: My good saw! And Nan's lamp, and three axes I'd written off. Ossie'll be glad. He's been sleeping with a lamp lit.

objectives.doneText: You pull the heap apart. Glass shards spill out from among stolen lamps, axe heads and a saw blade, all polished bright.

text.offer: Shrines are down, and they're still digging. Ossie heard them, the night he was in there. Chanting a name. The Glowmother. She's at the back, in a chamber they broke into, all cut stone and glass. And there's another name they say, lower: the Wickfather. Below, they say. I don't like the sound of either. Kill her, and bring me her crown so I know it's done.
text.summary: Kill the Glowmother in the glass chamber, at the back of the diggings, and bring Foreman Tarrant her glass crown.
text.waiting: The back of the diggings. Follow the glow.
text.done: That's it, then. Glass and wire. Warm, too. I'll keep this somewhere the Council won't look. Wickfather. You didn't see anything, did you? Below?

text.offer: One tunnel runs on past where they've been bowing. Past the glass chamber, Ossie says, down and down. They were still digging it. I'll not send a logger down there. Go to the end of it and tell me what they were digging toward.
text.summary: Go to the end of the deepest tunnel in the diggings, past the glass chamber, and tell Foreman Tarrant what you find.
text.waiting: Past the chamber, down to the end. Then come straight back.
text.done: Singing. Right. No. I'll have stone hauled up and it'll be walled shut before the week's out, and nobody goes past the chamber again. Not for glass, not for anything.

objectives.doneText: The tunnel ends at a fall of fresh rock. Cold, wet air comes through the gaps, smelling of deep water. You put your ear to the stones. Far behind them, something is singing, one long low note, and then another.

text.offer: Chute's stopped. Every time a man goes up to the head of it, arrows come down off the cliff top. Never hit anyone. Not yet. But no one'll go up, and the quota's due. You go. The chute's head is up the slope, north of camp, under the cliff. See what they're shooting at.
text.summary: Climb to the chute's head, north of Cliffside camp under the cliff, and find what the arrows are aimed at.
text.waiting: Up the slope behind camp. Keep your head down.
text.done: The stumps. Only the stumps, the newest cut, every arrow. Not one in a man, not one in the chute. Somebody up there's telling us something. I wish they'd just say it.

objectives.doneText: Another stump, cut this season, the sap still wet. Three arrows stand in it, fletched with grey feathers, in a tight ring round the heart of the wood.

text.offer: I'd rather know what they want than lose a man finding out. I've written it down. Take it up to the chute's head and wait. If they're watching the stumps, they'll see you.
text.summary: Take Foreman Tarrant's message to the chute's head, north of the camp, and wait for whoever comes down.
text.waiting: Up to the chute's head. Hold it up where they can see it, I suppose.
text.done: "No man of mine will lift a bow." He writes like a man who means it. I am Ithriel. I keep the high forest, and I have watched your foreman's people cut it for two summers. I did not come down to bargain. I came down to show you something.

text.offer: The trees on this slope are not standing on the cliff. They are holding it. Their roots go down into every crack, and the rock hangs on them. Where your loggers have cut, the roots die, and the rock lets go. You will not take my word for it. Go and look, along the slope's top, at the ground that has slumped since the cutting began.
text.summary: Look at 3 places along the top of the slope by the chute's head where the ground has slumped.
text.waiting: Along the slope, under the cliff. Look where the stumps are.
text.done: Now you have seen it. Next spring it will be larger, and the spring after, a piece of that cliff will come down on your foreman's camp. I would rather not watch that.

objectives.doneText: A lip of earth has broken away and slid, taking stones with it. Dead roots hang out of the scar like cut string, and above them a crack runs up into the cliff.

text.offer: This cord is the line. Below it, your foreman may cut what he likes. Above it, not one tree. Where it turns, I have tied a leaf, and I will put my own marks on the trunks tonight. Take it to him. Tell him what you saw. If the line holds, the arrows stop.
text.summary: Take Ithriel's marked cord to Foreman Tarrant, and tell him where her line runs and what you saw on the ledge.
text.waiting: Take it down to him. I will be watching.
text.done: A line. Above it, nothing. Do you know what that does to the quota? The Council will have my hide. ...And a cliff on the cook tent would cost more than a short year. Fine. Fine! Tell her the line holds. Gods, I need a drink.

text.offer: Damp up here rots hemp in a month, and a rope that goes on the chute drops a log on someone. Spider silk doesn't rot. The big spiders at the cliff foot, south of camp, spin it thick as your finger. Nobody here'll go near them. Would you?
text.summary: Bring 6 coils of silk from the spiders at the cliff foot, south of Cliffside camp.
text.waiting: South along the cliff foot. Mind the webs.
text.done: Look at that. You could hang a bull from it. Nan'll braid it into a rope by tonight.

text.offer: Kobolds in the loggers' valley, west of here, have taken to marking our trees. Chalk, a scratch on every trunk we've felled and every one we haven't. Counting them, Dell says. What does a kobold count trees for? Bring me some of their tallies and let's see.
text.summary: Bring 5 chalk tallies from the kobolds in the loggers' valley, west of Cliffside camp.
text.waiting: They carry their tallies on sticks. West, in the valley.
text.done: One row for pine, one for oak, one for ash... and this one. That's us. A mark for every logger. They're not counting trees. They're counting what we take, and who takes it. Someone taught them that.

text.offer: Hill wolves come down off the valley's edge at dusk and the wagon horses smell them a mile off. Last month a team bolted into the brook, wagon and all. Forty sacks, gone downstream. The Council asked me whether the wolves had grey coats on too. Thin them, would you? Along the valley's edge, south of the hall.
text.summary: Kill 8 wolves along the valley's edge, south of Tennely Hall.
text.waiting: South of the hall, along the edge of the trees. They're bold at dusk.
text.done: Eight. The carters will thank you, even if they won't say it. Carters never say it.

text.offer: Varn's ledger says a tenth extra came up the grain road to me. It didn't. I keep my count to the sack, and I'll not be called a thief by a clerk's column. Here's my wagon book. The granary is across the courtyard, three bays. Count them against the book yourself, and then tell me I'm lying.
text.summary: Count the sacks in the granary's 3 bays, across the courtyard, against Captain Hale's wagon book.
text.waiting: Up the steps, three bays. Take your time. I have.
text.done: To the sack. What the Council asked, and not one more. So the tenth left Brightford, and it never got here. Somewhere on that road, it went somewhere else.

objectives.doneText: You count the north bay twice. It matches the wagon book to the sack.
The middle bay matches the book too, down to a half-sack Hale has noted as "split, rat".
The south bay matches. Every sack the Council asked for is here, and not one more.

text.offer: Some wagons come in light, and late. Light I can explain: robbers. Late, I can't, not with the robbers working the north road. There are fresh ruts that turn off the grain road a mile south of here, west into the trees, where no road goes. Follow them for me. I want to know where my sacks go before I write to the Council.
text.summary: Follow the wagon ruts that turn west off the grain road, south of Tennely Hall, over the saddle in the rise, to where they meet the north road.
text.waiting: South down the grain road, then west where the ruts go. Over the rise and down.
text.done: The north road. And from there it's a short haul to Northgate, where the Nordish traders pay in silver and ask no questions. So it isn't only Slade. Someone in a Council carter's coat drives my sacks over that saddle at night. I'll write this down. Carefully.

objectives.text: Where the ruts leave the grain road
objectives.doneText: Fresh wheel ruts turn off the road here, deep under a full load. A sack has split on a stone, and grain is spilled along the ruts into the trees.
At the top of the saddle a wagon has cast a wheel and left it. The ruts go on west, down the far side, with one rut shallower than the other.

objectives.text: Where the ruts meet the north road
objectives.doneText: The ruts end at the north road, at a heap of sacks under a tarp. The sacks are stamped with the Council's mark, and the road beyond runs north to Northgate.

text.offer: Robbers in grey coats have taken two of my wagons this month. Grey coats. The Council says Greycoats, and I've been told to say the same. I'd rather have proof. There's a watch post in the hills east of here, above the grain road, and the man who keeps it counts every wagon that's taken. Kill him and bring me what he counts on.
text.summary: Kill Slade's tallyman at the watch post in the hills east of Tennely Hall, above the grain road, and bring back his tally board.
text.waiting: East, up in the hills over the grain road. Look for the lookout.
text.done: A notch for every wagon. And this, burned in the back: a shelf in the hills, with a tent. Slade. I knew the name. I didn't know where he slept.

text.offer: I can't take the garrison off the granary. The Council would call it desertion before we were through the gate. But you're not the garrison. Slade's band camps on that shelf, east in the hills. Thin it out. Slade will have to come out of his tent himself.
text.summary: Kill 10 of Slade's band at his camp, on the shelf in the hills east of Tennely Hall.
text.waiting: Up on the shelf. They'll see you coming, so don't stop.
text.done: Ten. He'll be out of his tent now, and angry. Good.

text.offer: Slade keeps his own tally, in a book, and the book on him. Every wagon, every sack, and who bought them. Kill him and bring me that book, and I'll have proof of who's been wearing grey.
text.summary: Kill Slade at his command tent, at the east end of his camp in the hills, and bring Captain Hale his tally book.
text.waiting: His tent's at the east end of the shelf. He'll have guards.
text.done: Every wagon. Every sack. Sold on to Northgate, and to a carter with a Council seal. And not one Greycoat named in it. Not one. They've been blamed for all of it.

text.offer: If I send this to the Council, it goes in a drawer. If I take it where it belongs myself, I'm hanged. So you'll take it. There's a hunting lodge in the woods south-east of here, off the road. The Tennelys' once. Burned in the revolution. Someone camps there who'll know what to do with this. Tell her Wystan sent it. And don't tell anyone where you went.
text.summary: Take Slade's tally book to Captain Elsbet Rook at the burned hunting lodge, in the woods south-east of Tennely Hall.
text.waiting: South-east, in the trees, off the road. Go quietly.
text.done: Wystan sent this? Then he hasn't forgotten. Every Greycoat cleared, in a robber's own hand. Thank you. I've carried something for a long time that I can't keep any longer. This letter names the Tennelys' heir. The Council would burn it, and whoever holds it. Keep it safe for me. Keep it hidden.
